old_caption: The video begins with a close-up view of a light wooden surface, likely a table or workbench, set against a plain white background. A pair of hands, clad in gray sleeves, enter the frame from both sides. The hands move towards the center of the wooden surface, where two small, rectangular blocks of wood are placed. The hands then position themselves on either side of the blocks, fingers spread out, as if preparing to manipulate them. The hands immediately begin to adjust the position of the blocks. The hands then lift and place a long wooden plank across the two blocks, adjusting its position. The hands then move away from the plank.
original_wisa_caption: The video begins with a close-up view of a light wooden surface, likely a table or workbench, set against a plain white background. A pair of hands, clad in gray sleeves, enter the frame from both sides. The hands move towards the center of the wooden surface, where a small, rectangular block of wood is placed. The hands then position themselves on either side of the block, fingers spread out, as if preparing to manipulate it. The hands remain stationary for a moment, suggesting a pause in action. The scene is well-lit, emphasizing the natural texture of the wood and the smoothness of the hands' movements. There are no other objects or characters present in the video, and the focus remains solely on the interaction between the hands and the wooden block. The video captures a simple yet deliberate action, highlighting the precision and care involved in handling the materials.
caption: An overhead view shows a pale pine panel lying flat on a white tabletop. A pair of hands carries two small rectangular wooden blocks in from below and sets them on the panel, one on the left third and one on the right third, before releasing and withdrawing. The two blocks then rest at fixed positions on the bare surface. A long flat slat appears lying across the front edge of the panel. It is then shifted backward and upward until it rests on top of the blocks, elevated above the surface, while two hands grip its ends to hold and fine-tune this position before withdrawing. A second, rounded-edge slat is then brought in from below and laid flat on the panel in front of the blocks. The hands keep holding its two ends and adjust it through the final frames. Throughout, the panel and the two blocks stay put as the slats and hands move relative to them.
